checklist.evidence: Latency budget (p99): feature fetch 10 ms, model 3 ms, rules 2 ms, overhead 5 ms, with 30 ms of headroom.
a hard timeout on the scorer, then rules only, then default approve under a capped amount. Every fallback is logged and alerted on.
define each feature once in a feature platform (Feast, Tecton, or in-house) and log the exact feature vector served with every decision
only train on transactions old enough for labels to have arrived, for example more than 90 days ... out-of-time splits only, never random splits
decline if p(fraud) × amount × loss_rate > cost_of_false_decline ... PR-AUC, recall at a fixed decline rate
Rules are versioned, analysts can deploy them in minutes ... approve / decline / step-up (3DS/OTP) / review
Case management (analyst queue) ──► labels ... cardholder fraud claims (faster), and analyst decisions
Tokenize the full card number (PAN) at the edge so the fraud stack sees only tokens. This keeps most of the stack out of PCI scope.
use watermarks and handle late or out-of-order events. Deduplicate on transaction ID, because auth retries and reversals happen.
shadow mode (score everything, act on nothing, 2–4 weeks) → canary at 1–5% of traffic → champion/challenger ... feature null rate and drift (PSI)
keep audit logs of every decision with the model, rule, and feature versions ... SHAP-based reason codes for each decline
About 5–10k TPS at peak ... multi-AZ and active-active across regions. The online store is replicated.
